checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-016: Does parse_deposit_requests enforce two-layer deposit event filtering?

audit_items.state_context: Two separate deposit pipelines: ETH1 log path with two-layer filtering; EIP-6110 execution layer path with no within-batch deduplication. lastReceivedMerkleIndex is not consulted by ProcessDepositRequests. processingLock not held in EIP-6110 path.
audit_items.reasoning: The ETH1 log path correctly enforces two-layer filtering. However, the EIP-6110 path (ProcessDepositRequests/processDepositRequest) has NO within-batch deduplication. A malicious block proposer can include the same DepositRequest twice in ExecutionRequests.Deposits and both will be accepted, resulting in double-credit of pending deposits. Additionally, the ETH1 log path accesses Topics[0] without a length guard, causing a panic (DoS) if a zero-topics log reaches ProcessLog - possible from a malicious or buggy EL client since the FilterQuery only filters by contract address, not by topic.

phase1.summary: Two separate deposit pipelines discovered. ETH1 path has two-layer filtering; EIP-6110 path has no within-payload deduplication. Topics[0] accessed without length guard in ProcessLog at line 97.
phase1.abstract_state: ETH1 path: lastReceivedMerkleIndex tracks processed indices; strict sequential ordering enforced. EIP-6110 path: state mutated via AppendPendingDeposit for each entry in the input slice with no cross-entry deduplication.
anomalies: ProcessDepositRequests/processDepositRequest has no deduplication within a single block's ExecutionRequests.Deposits slice
Topics[0] accessed without len(Topics) check in ProcessLog at line 97
lastReceivedMerkleIndex not shared with EIP-6110 pipeline
processingLock not acquired in EIP-6110 path

attack_scenarios.name: Double-deposit via EIP-6110 duplicate DepositRequest
attack_scenarios.description: A malicious block proposer constructs a block where ExecutionRequests.Deposits contains the same deposit request twice (same index, pubkey, amount). ProcessDepositRequests iterates the slice without deduplication. processDepositRequest is called twice, appending the same deposit to pending_deposits twice. The depositor's balance is double-credited.
attack_scenarios.inputs: ExecutionRequests.Deposits = [{pubkey: P, amount: A, index: I, ...}, {pubkey: P, amount: A, index: I, ...}]

attack_scenarios.name: DoS via zero-topics log in ProcessLog
attack_scenarios.description: A malicious or buggy EL client returns a FilterLogs response with a log from the deposit contract address that has zero Topics. ProcessLog accesses Topics[0] unconditionally at line 97, causing an index-out-of-range panic in the beacon node ETH1 processing goroutine.
attack_scenarios.inputs: FilterLogs returns a Log with empty Topics slice from depositContractAddr

phase2_5.summary: A1 reachability: entry via block processing (Electra transition.go calling ProcessBlockForStateRoot -> ProcessOperations -> ... -> ProcessDepositRequests). Requires malicious block proposer role. A2 reachability: entry via ProcessETH1Block -> ProcessLog. FilterQuery uses address-only filter, no topic filter set. Requires malicious or buggy EL client.
phase2_5.reachability: A1: reachable with block proposer role. A2: reachable from EL interface with address-matching non-DepositEvent log.

phase3.summary: ETH1 path sequential index enforcement is sound but only protects against replay after ABI decode and topic check succeed. It does not protect the Topics[0] access. EIP-6110 path has no invariant protecting against within-payload duplicate requests. The spec (EIP-6110 / Electra process_deposit_request) relies on the EL to deduplicate, but the CL provides no additional safety net against a malicious proposer.
phase3.invariant_analysis: Broken: 'Each deposit request is processed at most once per block' - no within-payload index uniqueness check in processDepositRequest. Broken: 'Topics slice is non-empty before access' - no len(Topics) guard at ProcessLog line 97.

phase3_5.summary: A1 (double-deposit): bug_bounty_eligible=true, severity=High. A2 (Topics panic): bug_bounty_eligible=true, severity=Medium.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-016: Does extract_deposit_data validate 576-byte length and offsets?

audit_items.state_context: ABI decoder (go-ethereum) validates structural encoding (offsets within bounds, data present for each dynamic field). It does NOT validate semantic length constraints for dynamic `bytes` fields (pubkey must be 48 bytes, withdrawal_credentials 32 bytes, amount 8 bytes, signature 96 bytes, index 8 bytes). Downstream consumers assume fixed field sizes.
audit_items.reasoning: UnpackDepositLogData delegates all validation to the go-ethereum ABI decoder. The ABI decoder validates structural ABI encoding (offsets, data presence) but does NOT enforce semantic field lengths for dynamic `bytes` fields. A malicious or buggy EL client can supply a DepositEvent log where the `index` field is encoded as fewer than 8 bytes. The ABI decoder accepts this and returns a short []byte. ProcessDepositLog then calls binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(merkleTreeIndex) which panics (buffer too small) on any slice shorter than 8 bytes. Similarly, bytesutil.FromBytes8(amount) is assumed to be 8 bytes. This is a DoS vector against the beacon node's ETH1 log processing goroutine reachable from the EL interface.

phase1.summary: No explicit 576-byte length pre-check. Validation fully delegated to go-ethereum ABI decoder. ABI decoder enforces structural encoding but not semantic field lengths for dynamic bytes types. Type assertions at line 23 will panic on unexpected types (bounded by hardcoded ABI). Downstream code assumes fixed field sizes not validated at this boundary.
phase1.abstract_state: Post-ABI-decode: five []byte slices returned. No postcondition enforcement on lengths of returned slices. Downstream: binary.LittleEndian.Uint64 assumes index >= 8 bytes; bytesutil.FromBytes8 assumes amount >= 8 bytes.
anomalies: No field-level length validation after ABI decode for index (must be 8 bytes), amount (must be 8 bytes), pubkey (must be 48 bytes), signature (must be 96 bytes), withdrawal_credentials (must be 32 bytes)
binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(merkleTreeIndex) will panic if index field < 8 bytes
ABI parser constructed on every call (performance issue, but not a security issue)

phase2.summary: Concrete DoS attack via short index field.

attack_scenarios.name: Panic via short index field in DepositEvent ABI encoding
attack_scenarios.description: A malicious or buggy EL client returns a FilterLogs response where the DepositEvent log data contains a valid ABI structure but the `index` field is encoded as a dynamic bytes slice of length < 8 bytes (e.g., length = 0 or length = 4). The go-ethereum ABI decoder accepts this as structurally valid (it only validates that offset + length does not exceed buffer end). UnpackDepositLogData returns a short slice as merkleTreeIndex. ProcessDepositLog calls binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(merkleTreeIndex) which panics with 'runtime error: index out of range'. The ETH1 log processing goroutine crashes.
attack_scenarios.inputs: DepositEvent ABI encoding with index field: offset=<valid>, length=4, data=0x01020304

attack_scenarios.name: Invalid pubkey length bypassing BLS pre-check
attack_scenarios.description: A malicious block proposer supplies a deposit log with a pubkey field encoded as 0 bytes or non-48 bytes. ABI decoder accepts it. UnpackDepositLogData returns an empty or wrong-length pubkey. Downstream BLS signature verification may return an error rather than panic, but the exact behavior depends on the BLS library's handling of invalid key lengths. At minimum this causes processing noise; at worst a panic if the BLS library does not validate key length.
attack_scenarios.inputs: DepositEvent ABI encoding with pubkey field: length=0

phase2_5.summary: B1 reachability: FilterLogs is called from ProcessETH1Block with address-only filter. EL controls the content of log responses. Malicious EL client or EL implementation bug can supply crafted log data. Entry: ETH1 sync loop -> ProcessETH1Block -> ProcessLog -> ProcessDepositLog -> UnpackDepositLogData returns short index -> binary.LittleEndian.Uint64 panics.
phase2_5.reachability: Reachable from EL JSON-RPC interface. Requires malicious or buggy EL client. Severity: crashes beacon node ETH1 processing.

phase3.summary: Invariant 'index field is exactly 8 bytes' is not enforced at the UnpackDepositLogData boundary. The ABI decoder does not enforce this constraint for dynamic bytes fields. The downstream consumer (binary.LittleEndian.Uint64) is not defensive. The guard is insufficient: ABI structural validation does not imply semantic field length correctness.
phase3.invariant_analysis: Broken: 'len(merkleTreeIndex) >= 8' is not guaranteed by UnpackDepositLogData. 'len(amount) >= 8' is not guaranteed. These invariants are assumed by downstream code but not enforced at the boundary.

phase3_5.summary: bug_bounty_eligible=true. Missing post-ABI-decode field length validation for index and amount fields. A malformed DepositEvent log from the EL interface causes a panic (DoS) in beacon node ETH1 processing.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-017: Is compute_requests_hash deterministic across all clients?

audit_items.state_context: Prysm serializes ExecutionRequests via EncodeExecutionRequests in proto/engine/v1/electra.go: SSZ-encodes each request type with a type-byte prefix, omits empty lists, maintains fixed type order. This is passed to EL as flattenedRequests []hexutil.Bytes over engine_newPayloadV4 JSON-RPC. EL computes SHA256-based requests_hash per EIP-7685.
audit_items.reasoning: Prysm does not compute requests_hash itself - it delegates to the execution layer per the EIP-7685 / Electra architecture. Prysm's EncodeExecutionRequests is deterministic: SSZ serialization is deterministic for fixed-size fields, type ordering is fixed (deposits=0, withdrawals=1, consolidations=2), and empty type entries are consistently omitted per EIP-7685 specification. The nil ExecutionRequests guard is present. No Prysm-side non-determinism was found. Cross-client hash divergence would only arise from other CL clients encoding differently from the spec, which is not attributable to Prysm. The version-dispatch edge case (V3 vs V4 selection) is an informational note but does not represent an exploitable bug in the current code paths for Electra blocks.

phase1.summary: Prysm delegates requests_hash computation entirely to the EL via engine_newPayloadV4. EncodeExecutionRequests produces a deterministic encoding: SSZ for each request type, fixed type order, empty types omitted. Nil requests guard present in notifyNewPayload.
phase1.abstract_state: requests: *enginev1.ExecutionRequests (non-nil enforced). EncodeExecutionRequests: deterministic mapping from structured requests to []hexutil.Bytes. EL receives consistent encoding from Prysm.
anomalies: Cross-client non-determinism if other CL clients include explicit zero-length type entries that Prysm omits (spec says omit empty types; Prysm follows spec)
Version dispatch selects V4 when executionRequests != nil and payload type is ExecutionPayloadDeneb - edge case noted but no concrete exploit path found

phase2.summary: No exploitable Prysm-internal non-determinism found. Cross-client scenarios depend on other clients' non-conformance.

attack_scenarios.name: Cross-client non-determinism from empty type inclusion
attack_scenarios.description: If another CL client includes explicit zero-length type-byte entries for empty request types in the flattenedRequests list while Prysm omits them, the EL receives different inputs from different CL clients and computes different requests_hash values. This would cause consensus divergence. However, EIP-7685 specifies that empty request types should be omitted, making Prysm's behavior correct and any divergence attributable to the other client.
attack_scenarios.inputs: N/A - depends on other client behavior

phase2_5.summary: No reachable exploit from Prysm internals. Cross-client scenario requires non-conforming peer implementation. Prysm's implementation correctly follows EIP-7685.
phase2_5.reachability: Not reachable via Prysm internals alone.

phase3.summary: Invariant 'requests_hash is deterministic for a given block' holds within Prysm's implementation. SSZ determinism + fixed type order + consistent empty-type omission ensures Prysm always produces the same flattenedRequests for the same block content. EL hash computation is deterministic given the same input.
phase3.invariant_analysis: Satisfied: EncodeExecutionRequests is a deterministic function of its inputs. Nil guard ensures requests != nil before encoding. Type order is fixed in implementation. Empty types consistently omitted per spec.

phase3_5.summary: bug_bounty_eligible=false for primary concern (hash determinism). Prysm's implementation is correct per EIP-7685. No Prysm-side vulnerability found.
